product: Porch is a homeowners insurance company built on vertical software. Insurance Services operates through the Porch Reciprocal Exchange and HOA, including Porch Insurance launched January 2026; Software and Data sells subscription software to inspection, mortgage, title and roofing companies; Consumer Services sells moving and other home services.
demand: Q2 2026 Reciprocal Policies Written rose 38% YoY, quote volume rose 87%, agency branch locations rose 148%, and RWP from new customers rose 206%. Offsetting this, the Software and Data company base shrank 22% YoY to 18.7 thousand and Consumer Services monetized services fell 4%.
pricing_power: Insurance Services gross margin was 87% and Insurance Services Adjusted EBITDA was 32% of RWP, up from 16%, showing strong fee economics. But RWP per policy written fell 16% to $2,383 as new-policy premiums are lower than renewals, and Texas rate and form changes need regulatory approval, so pricing power on new business looks limited.
competition: The company frames itself against incumbent homeowners insurance carriers and traditional distribution, and cites risk of disruption in independent agency relationships and products not meeting customer demand. No named competitor appears in the filings read. Agency branch count up 148% and quotes up 87% indicate expanding distribution reach rather than disclosed share data.
team: Matt Ehrlichman is Chief Executive Officer, Chairman and Founder; Shawn Tabak is Chief Financial Officer and signed the 2026-06-11 Form 8-K. Directors were elected at the 2026-06-15 annual meeting. Director Amanda L Reierson sold 33,135 shares at $16.4573 on 2026-09-14 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan.
market_strategy: Deploy vertical software in home-related industries, use proprietary data for advantaged underwriting, expand the state footprint (HOA in 22 states after the Michigan launch), and scale Reciprocal policy count and statutory surplus. Porch keeps capital-light fee economics through the Reciprocal while the Reciprocal owns the underwriting entity HOA and its policyholder-members own the Reciprocal.
bull: Q2 2026 (2026-07-29): revenue $140.9M +12% YoY, Insurance Services $92.9M +38%, Adjusted EBITDA ex-Reciprocal $39.1M +150%, FY26 guidance raised to $506-517M revenue and $119-125M EBITDA; five dated raises in 90 days.
bear: Reciprocal gross margin fell 57% to 38% YoY on higher loss retention, RWP per policy -16%, Software and Data company count -22%, net income only $5.6M, Texas 56-57% of revenue, director sold 33,135 shares at $16.4573 on 2026-09-14.
falsifier: Q3 2026 results (est. 2026-11-04) showing Reciprocal statutory surplus below $169.9M or policy growth decelerating from 38% YoY would prove the bull case wrong.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 results 2026-07-29: revenue $140.9M up 12% YoY, Porch-owned revenue $131.8M up 23%, Insurance Services $92.9M up 38%, net income attributable to Porch $5.6M, Adjusted EBITDA ex-Reciprocal $39.1M up 150%, and FY26 guidance raised to $506-517M revenue and $119-125M Adjusted EBITDA. On 2026-06-11 Porticus bought 2.1M shares from the Reciprocal at $7.17; July 2026 added about $100M catastrophe bond.
web_not_known_yesterday: Nothing new dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25. The latest press release was the 2026-08-11 investor-events notice. Newest filings are Form 144s filed 2026-09-14 and a Form 4 filed 2026-09-16 showing director Amanda Reierson sold 33,135 shares at $16.4573 on 2026-09-14 under a 10b5-1 plan; Cantor and Oppenheimer non-deal roadshows were 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and demand led: Reciprocal Policies Written up 38% YoY to 58.7 thousand, agency branches up 148%, quotes up 87%, and RWP from new customers up 206%. Pricing and mix drag: RWP per policy written fell 16% to $2,383 and total RWP rose only 16%. Software and Data is price led, revenue per company up 24% while company count fell 22%.
web_suppliers: Reinsurance capacity is the key input. The third-party excess-of-loss panel effective 2026-04-01 runs from $35.0M per occurrence to $365.0M, plus about $100M of collateralized catastrophe bond placed July 2026, with captive Porticus Reinsurance Ltd taking quota share. One reinsurer is 14% of reinsurance balance due. Reciprocal surplus was $169.9M, supporting over $800M of RWP; management calls capacity strong but retention rose.
web_customers: Insurance Services is paid mainly by the Reciprocal: management fees on RWP, policy fees per policy, captive reinsurance premiums and lead fees. 56-57% of consolidated revenue comes from Texas customers. Software and Data serves about 18.7 thousand inspection, mortgage, title and roofing companies, down 22% YoY, and Consumer Services about 83.9 thousand monetized services. Unsecured Reciprocal receivables are a stated credit concentration.
web_who_loses: Incumbent homeowners carriers and their agency distribution lose share if the Reciprocal keeps writing policies, especially in Texas. Third-party reinsurers receive less ceded premium because the April 2026 program cedes a smaller loss share. Legacy paid-lead home services marketplaces lose as Porch routes demand through its own software and agencies. This is inference from the 10-Q, not a company statement.
web_contradicting_evidence: Reciprocal gross margin fell from 57% to 38% YoY as it retains more loss. RWP per policy written fell 16%. Software and Data company count fell 22%. Consolidated revenue grew 12% versus 23% for Porch-owned segments. Net income attributable to Porch was only $5.6M, and the Reciprocal is not owned by Porch. Texas is 56-57% of revenue. KBW is Hold at $17, one sell rating exists, and a director sold shares 2026-09-14.
web_if_management_right: FY26 guidance of $506-517M revenue and $119-125M Adjusted EBITDA ex-Reciprocal is met or beaten, policy growth stays near 38%, statutory surplus keeps building from $169.9M to support over $800M of RWP, leverage stays under 3x, net income stays positive, and the growing insurance-services mix keeps lifting margins and re-rating the shares.
web_if_management_wrong: First to break is Reciprocal capital and reinsurance: retaining more loss plus a large catastrophe erodes statutory surplus, forces more support from the captive whose capital and collateral are tied to the PRCH share price, and stalls policy growth, cutting management fees and Insurance Services revenue. Software and Data churn and 56-57% Texas concentration amplify the damage.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Reinsurers on the excess-of-loss panel and catastrophe-bond and ILS investors that supplied the July 2026 $100M cover gain as RWP scales toward and beyond $800M of capacity. Independent insurance agencies gain commissions as branch count rose 148%. Inspection, mortgage, title and roofing software partners gain volume as Porch embeds their data and distribution.
